title: Go, your son lives (John 4:43–54)
hookLine: a royal official believes the word and walks home
tomorrow: do you want to be healed?

lines: A KING'S OFFICIAL, A DYING SON.
COME DOWN ERE MY CHILD DIE.
cards: A man with rank, and none of it helps. The King James calls him a nobleman, an official of the king, and his son is at the point of death in Capernaum.
He hears Jesus is back in Galilee, at Cana, the village of the wedding, and goes up to find him. Every hour he's gone is an hour he's not at his son's bed. He doesn't make a speech.
He begs: "Sir, come down ere my child die." Come down. Come with me.

teach.b: Jesus's first answer sounds like a sigh, aimed at the whole crowd as much as at him: "Except ye see signs and wonders, ye will not believe." The father doesn't argue. He asks again.

teach.h: GO THY WAY; THY SON LIVETH.
teach.b: He says one short sentence: "Go thy way; thy son liveth." No touch, no visit, no proof. Then John writes today's line: "And the man believed the word that Jesus had spoken unto him, and he went his way."

teach.h: A LONG ROAD WITH ONLY A SENTENCE.
teach.b: He begged Jesus to come, and he's leaving without him, carrying nothing but a sentence. The next day, still on the road, his servants run to meet him. Your son lives.
When did he start getting better?
"Yesterday at the seventh hour the fever left him." The very hour Jesus said go.
And John says the man believed, and his whole household with him. The word believe appears twice. First he believes the word, enough to start walking.
Then, when he sees what happened, he believes in a fuller way: a step on trust, then sight. John counts this as the second sign Jesus did in Galilee, after the water turned to wine, both from Cana.
One at a wedding, one by a word spoken from a distance.

how: Some Christians turn to this story when someone they love is ill and far away, and some churches pray for the sick by name during worship.

o: Jesus's word sending a father home on trust
a command to leave and never come back
permission to go and find a better healer

games.q: what's inside John 4:43–54 — tap the pairs.
p: in the service of the king

s: Jesus went to Capernaum to heal the boy
he never went. he said "go thy way; thy son liveth" from Cana.
the father learned the fever broke at the hour Jesus spoke
the servants said the seventh hour, the moment of "go."
John calls this the first sign in Cana
it's the second; the first was the water turned to wine.

games.q: you're the father. you begged Jesus to come with you, and he says: go, your son lives. what do you do?
o: turn around and start the long walk home.
stay in Cana until you hear news.
games.why: "the man believed the word that Jesus had spoken unto him, and he went his way." the good news meets him on the road.

practice: Think of a word someone has given you that you can't check yet: a friend's I'll be there, a doctor's this will heal, a line from scripture you hold onto.

Notice whether part of you wants proof first, then picture taking the first step home anyway, with only the sentence in your pocket. If you pray, hold that word before God; if you don't, rest with it a moment.

wordCard.voice: Go. Jesus's answer to a desperate father: go thy way, thy son liveth. One word that sends him home on nothing but trust.

orig.note: Greek: go, be on your way. The first word of Jesus's answer in John 4:50.

carryVoice: Your line: he believed the word. The seeing came later, on the road. Six hundred four days in.
